finalText:
This is a small Node HTTP API, five files, no dependencies.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    server[server.js] --> auth[auth.js]
    server --> routes[routes.js]
    routes --> cache[cache.js]
    routes --> store[store.js]
    cache --> store
```

- `server.js` — starts the HTTP server, checks the request's token, then hands off to the router.
- `auth.js` — makes and checks bearer tokens. Each one is a user ID plus an HMAC signature, signed with `AUTH_SECRET`.
- `routes.js` — a small table mapping method and path to a handler. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to the store.
- `cache.js` — a 256-entry LRU cache sitting in front of the store, for repeated reads.
- `store.js` — the actual data. It's all in memory, and every record expires 15 minutes after it's written.

One sharp edge worth knowing: the comment in `routes.js` says writes should invalidate the cache, but `POST /orders` never does that. So after someone posts an order, a cached `orders:<id>` read can keep returning the old list until it's bumped out of the LRU.
